# Install tidyverse
#install.packages("tidyverse")

# Load the package
library(tidyverse)
## Warning: package 'ggplot2' was built under R version 4.6.2
## Warning: package 'dplyr' was built under R version 4.6.2

# Import the student dataset
student <- read.csv(file.choose())
#view(student)

# Check the dataset
head(student)
##   Hours.Studied Previous.Scores Extracurricular.Activities Sleep.Hours
## 1             7              99                        Yes           9
## 2             4              82                         No           4
## 3             8              51                        Yes           7
## 4             5              52                        Yes           5
## 5             7              75                         No           8
## 6             3              78                         No           9
##   Sample.Question.Papers.Practiced Performance.Index
## 1                                1                91
## 2                                2                65
## 3                                2                45
## 4                                2                36
## 5                                5                66
## 6                                6                61
tail(student)
##       Hours.Studied Previous.Scores Extracurricular.Activities Sleep.Hours
## 9995              6              46                        Yes           8
## 9996              1              49                        Yes           4
## 9997              7              64                        Yes           8
## 9998              6              83                        Yes           8
## 9999              9              97                        Yes           7
## 10000             7              74                         No           8
##       Sample.Question.Papers.Practiced Performance.Index
## 9995                                 0                39
## 9996                                 2                23
## 9997                                 5                58
## 9998                                 5                74
## 9999                                 0                95
## 10000                                1                64
str(student)
## 'data.frame':    10000 obs. of  6 variables:
##  $ Hours.Studied                   : int  7 4 8 5 7 3 7 8 5 4 ...
##  $ Previous.Scores                 : int  99 82 51 52 75 78 73 45 77 89 ...
##  $ Extracurricular.Activities      : chr  "Yes" "No" "Yes" "Yes" ...
##  $ Sleep.Hours                     : int  9 4 7 5 8 9 5 4 8 4 ...
##  $ Sample.Question.Papers.Practiced: int  1 2 2 2 5 6 6 6 2 0 ...
##  $ Performance.Index               : num  91 65 45 36 66 61 63 42 61 69 ...
# Remove duplicate observations
student_clean <- student[!duplicated(student), ]

# Convert extracurricular activities into a categorical variable
student_clean$Extracurricular.Activities <- as.factor(
  student_clean$Extracurricular.Activities
)

# Check the cleaned dataset
dim(student_clean)
## [1] 9873    6
#GEOBAR-BARCHART
ggplot(student_clean, aes(x = Extracurricular.Activities)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Students Participating in Extracurricular Activities",
       x = "Extracurricular Activities",
       y = "Number of Students")

#GeomBoxplot-BOXPLOT
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Extracurricular.Activities,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "lightblue") +
  labs(title = "Student Performance by Extracurricular Activities",
       x = "Extracurricular Activities",
       y = "Performance Index")

#GeomDensity-DENSITY PLOT
ggplot(student_clean, aes(x = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_density(fill = "lightgreen", alpha = 0.6) +
  labs(title = "Density Distribution of Student Performance",
       x = "Performance Index",
       y = "Density")

#geom_histogram() – Histogram
ggplot(student_clean, aes(x = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = "skyblue",
                 color = "black") +
  labs(title = "Distribution of Student Performance",
       x = "Performance Index",
       y = "Frequency")

#geom_hline() – Horizontal line
# Calculate average performance
mean_performance <- mean(student_clean$Performance.Index)

# Create histogram with average reference line
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Hours.Studied,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean_performance,
             color = "red", linewidth = 1)

#geom_jitter() – Jitter plot
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Extracurricular.Activities,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.3,
              color = "blue") +
  labs(title = "Student Performance by Activities",
       x = "Extracurricular Activities",
       y = "Performance Index")

#geom_line() – Line graph
# Calculate average performance for each study hour
student_summary <- aggregate(
  Performance.Index ~ Hours.Studied,
  data = student_clean,
  FUN = mean
)

# Create line graph
ggplot(student_summary,
       aes(x = Hours.Studied,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_line(color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Average Performance by Study Hours",
       x = "Hours Studied",
       y = "Average Performance")

#geom_point() – Scatter plot
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Hours.Studied,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Study Hours vs Student Performance",
       x = "Hours Studied",
       y = "Performance Index")

#geom_rug() – Rug plot
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Hours.Studied,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_rug(color = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Student Performance with Rug Plot",
       x = "Hours Studied",
       y = "Performance Index")

#geom_smooth() – Smooth trend line
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Hours.Studied,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Relationship Between Study Hours and Performance",
       x = "Hours Studied",
       y = "Performance Index")
## `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

#geom_text() – Add text labels
# Create a data frame for the label
label_data <- data.frame(
  x = mean(student_clean$Hours.Studied),
  y = mean(student_clean$Performance.Index),
  label = "Average Performance"
)

# Create scatter plot with text
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Hours.Studied,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_text(data = label_data,
            aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
            color = "red") +
  labs(title = "Student Performance with Text Annotation",
       x = "Hours Studied",
       y = "Performance Index")

#geom_violin() – Violin plot
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Extracurricular.Activities,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_violin(fill = "lightpink") +
  labs(title = "Performance Distribution by Activities",
       x = "Extracurricular Activities",
       y = "Performance Index")

#geom_vline() – Vertical line
# Calculate average study hours
mean_hours <- mean(student_clean$Hours.Studied)

# Create scatter plot with vertical reference line
ggplot(student_clean,
       aes(x = Hours.Studied,
           y = Performance.Index)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean_hours,
             color = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "Student Performance with Average Study Hours",
       x = "Hours Studied",
       y = "Performance Index")

class(student_clean)
